### [Great & scenic views!](https://www.tripadvisor.com/ShowUserReviews-g1118447-d323955-r867556448-Sounkyo_Gorge-Kamikawa_cho_Kamikawa_gun_Hokkaido.html)









Was trying to do a review for both Ginga and Ryusei waterfall but noted that Sounkyo Gorge just nice covered both plus surrounding area!

Our first itinerary for Day 2, reaching early about 8.15am and has the whole place to us… happy! Ginga and Ryusei Waterfalls are located in the Sounkyo Gorge and the name Ginga no Taki translates to “Milky Way Waterfall” and Ryusei no Taki means “Shooting Star Waterfall.”. One of the scenic spots in Daisetsuzan National Park they are a pair of waterfalls that is divided by a huge rock formation protruding from the cliff, and flowing down closely to each other. The Ginga Waterfall (Ginga-no-taki銀河の滝) and Ryusei Waterfall (Ryusei-no-taki 流星の滝\];) forms yet another set of twin Japanese waterfalls in the country. The water source for both of these waterfalls comes from Mount Daisetsu at the background.

Dynamic water falls from 90m high cliff to form the Ryuseia fall while the Ginga fall flows more elegantly but at a higher altitude more than 100m above. There are hiking trails that allow you to view the falls separately but we do not have the time/luxury to venture deeper due to tight schedule. But do watch out for the river flow amid the trees and rocks, equally paramount scenic for all!

Each year, many tourists come to see the autumnal foliage in the area. Where our coach parked there is a store, and near the store (nearer the Ginga Falls). WE have more than 30 mins admiring the wonderful scene, photos taking before moving off to Mt Kuradake. 😊

### [Lovely in autumn, but not as mind blowing as we had hoped](https://www.tripadvisor.com/ShowUserReviews-g1121426-d1397431-r691402258-Kankakei_Gorge-Shodoshima_cho_Shozu_gun_Shodo_shima_Kagawa_Prefecture_Shikoku.html)









We took the ropeway up and walked down which like to do in places such as this. We get two different experiences and two different views of everything. There is a separate review of the ropeway experience with its rock formations and colorful trees. There are two trails down, we took the longer western trail because it ended up right at the bus stop below the ropeway station.



We visited a few days before peak, though the Tourist Information Center told us the gorge was at peak. The colors were good, but by no means great. Some of the best color on the top was behind the toilet block which is worth a visit if only for its interesting design. The viewpoint east of the station also had some of the best color we saw on the summit. The view out to the coast was quite nice but we came for color not distant panoramas.



The summit was rather disappointing. Its main purpose seemed to be accommodating loads of tourist buses whose passengers wanted to shop, buy souvenirs or plants, and eat. There were a few lookout viewpoints which we searched out. We arrived early in the morning. As the morning progressed the place got more and more crowded.



The walk down was pretty exciting, with views of contorted and bizarre volcanic rock. There are many places where one could get mind blowing shots but some of the viewpoints looked very dangerous. We stuck to the path for most of the way down. There are signs, Japanese only, with photos of what can be seen in the rock formations if you look in the right direction. It took us a while to figure the signs out. The walk down was perhaps the best part of the visit. It took us an hour and 45 minutes to get to the bottom but we stopped for photography.



Once you return to the bottom, check the posted bus schedule and get in line. The line formed quickly beginning about a half hour before the bus was scheduled to arrive. There is only so much room on each bus, even with people standing, those at the back of the line had to wait for the next bus. We took turns holding our place in line whilst the other wandered around and took more photos. There were some very nice colorful trees around the edge of the parking lot and a small stream with a bridge.



Visitor's tips - go early, bring a snack, ropeway up and walk down.

### [Conspiracy Theories](https://www.tripadvisor.com/ShowUserReviews-g1023508-d1637747-r732925452-Settsukyo_Park-Takatsuki_Osaka_Prefecture_Kinki.html)









We visited this beautiful park on a Monday afternoon late in November to see the Autumn leaves. From here, you can reach Settsu Gorge, a hot spring and then follow a not-too-challenging trail to a 15-meter waterfall called Shirataki.



Settsukyo first opened to the public in 1968, and some of the abandoned buildings along the path to the waterfall look like they haven’t been occupied since then. In three hours of wandering around the park, we saw a grand total of two other people (and this is supposed to be peak season!). We came expecting beautiful autumn leaves and we certainly got that, but I wasn’t expecting the post-apocalyptic vibe that I got from the dilapidated buildings and spooky trails. I liked it.



Finally, there is a lot of wrong information about this place on the Internet. To get there, take a train to JR Takatsuki and then bus number 52 to Tsukawaki stop (double check with the driver). From there, you’re a 5-10 minute walk to the entrance. If you choose to hike to the waterfall, follow the Japanese signs on the ground rather than online maps. Both Google and Yahoo maps are wrong (and have different wrong locations). The Japanese sign you need to look out for is this :白滝 (Shirataki).



No less than four websites had wrong directions for Settsukyo. I even wondered if there was some kind of secret agenda to keep people away. If you can get in and out and see the waterfall, then it’s worth it. Achievement unlocked!

# Top 19 Gorges in Japan
## Best canyons in Japan
- The most popular canyons is [Iwaya-ji (Temple 45)](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/5771116), a religious building located on Kuma Highland in a gorge formed of conglomerate rock. This temple, at an altitude of 585 m, is considered one of the difficult-to-reach places in Ehime.
- Another must-see spot is [Rankyo Gorge](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/7386729), a dramatic gorge carved by the Hozugawa River between Kameoka and Arashiyama. It offers Kyoto's natural scenery, which can be experienced via a traditional boat ride or a scenic train.
- Visitors also love [Narrow Rock Passage](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/732803), a challenging gorge. Visitors note it is a fun experience, though it can be muddy after rain.
- The canyons in Japan are appreciated by the komoot community, with 19 highlights featuring 19 photos and 10 upvotes.

## Frequently Asked Questions
Japan offers several dramatic canyons. [Kurobe Gorge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurobe_Gorge) in Toyama Prefecture is known as one of the deepest V-shaped gorges, offering steep cliffs and untouched forests. Ryujin Gorge in Ibaraki Prefecture is home to one of Japan's longest pedestrian suspension bridges, offering panoramic views.

Some, like [Rankyo Gorge](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/7386729), are carved by rivers and offer spectacular views of rugged mountains and rapids.

Kurobe Gorge is popular for its scenic railway, the Kurobe Gorge Railway, which provides a comfortable way to see the gorge. Sandankyo Gorge has well-maintained walking trails suitable for various fitness levels, and boat tours are available in areas like Kurobuchi. Hatonosu Canyon in Tokyo also offers a promenade and refreshing waters for swimming in summer.

Minakami in Gunma Prefecture is considered a premier canyoning destination globally, offering courses from family-friendly to adrenaline-pumping. Nametoko Gorge in Shikoku and Kamoshika Canyon in Hakuba (Nagano Prefecture) are also renowned for their canyoning opportunities, featuring slides, waterfall descents, and swimming in deep pools.

The Ryujin Suspension Bridge in Ryujin Gorge provides panoramic views of the gorge, surrounding mountain ranges, and even the Mito cityscape. The Kami-no-Iwahashi Bridge in Dakigaeri Gorge, Akita's oldest suspension bridge, also provides excellent vantage points. For a challenging view, [Sanpuku-gake Cliff](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/6831609) offers a dramatic perspective.

Many enjoy the thrill of boat rides through gorges like [Rankyo Gorge](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/7386729) or the scenic train journey through Kurobe Gorge.

Many are deep V-shaped gorges, like [Kurobe Gorge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurobe_Gorge), carved through mountainous terrain.

Hatonosu Canyon in Tokyo is noted for its refreshing, cold waters, making it a great spot for swimming during the summer.

# Top 19 Gorges in Japan

Canyons in Japan are found across a diverse landscape, from deep V-shaped gorges in mountain ranges to serene valleys within urban areas. The country's geology, shaped by rivers and tectonic activity, has created numerous dramatic natural formations. These areas often feature steep cliffs, clear waters, and dense forests, providing varied natural environments. Japan's canyons offer a range of experiences, from accessible walking trails to challenging routes.


## Best canyons in Japan

- The most popular canyons is [Iwaya-ji (Temple 45)](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/5771116), a religious building located on Kuma Highland in a gorge formed of conglomerate rock. This temple, at an altitude of 585 m, is considered one of the difficult-to-reach places in Ehime.

- Another must-see spot is [Rankyo Gorge](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/7386729), a dramatic gorge carved by the Hozugawa River between Kameoka and Arashiyama. It offers Kyoto's natural scenery, which can be experienced via a traditional boat ride or a scenic train.

- Visitors also love [Narrow Rock Passage](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/732803), a challenging gorge. Visitors note it is a fun experience, though it can be muddy after rain.

- Japan is known for its river gorges, deep valleys, and narrow rock passages. These areas offer a variety of landscapes to see and explore, from tranquil walks to more demanding routes.

- The canyons in Japan are appreciated by the komoot community, with 19 highlights featuring 19 photos and 10 upvotes.

[**Iwaya-ji (Temple 45)**](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/5771116)

Highlight • Religious Site

Iwaya-ji is temple No. 45 on the Shikoku Pilgrimage, or Henro. If there’s one temple on the pilgrimage you really should visit in Ehime Prefecture, Iwaya-ji is it. The temple is located on Kuma Highland in a gorge formed of conglomerate rock. It inspires awe, from the trek up the hillside, to its location embedded in a pock-marked cliff, and the beauty of its structures. At an altitude of 585 m, this temple is one of the nansho (difficult to reach places) of Ehime and mountain recluses and wandering holy men once performed their religious disciplines among the cliffs here.

[**Geibikei Gorge**](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/2214195)

Highlight • Gorge

I was there on a day that it was raining and had been raining for quite a while. I just meant that the water through the gorge was not fully staying within the banks, and made for some impressive drama. I did a quick ride by as I'm planning on going back tomorrow. There are two walking loops along the edge of the gorge that are not bike-friendly. There's a very narrow suspension bridge for pedestrians only that you should probably do for the best view of the gorge and the larger waterfall. Apparently there's also dango that gets sent across the gorge on a rope? A friend told me to be sure to have some, but I was there after hours today so that's on the plan for tomorrow.

The Hozugawa River Gorge (Rankyo) is the dramatic canyon carved by the Hozugawa River between Kameoka and Arashiyama. It is worth visiting because it offers Kyoto's most spectacular natural scenery, which is best experienced via the traditional Hozugawa River Boat Ride or the scenic Sagano Torokko Train. ## Frequently Asked Questions

What are some of the most dramatic canyons in Japan?

Japan offers several dramatic canyons. [Kurobe Gorge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurobe_Gorge) in Toyama Prefecture is known as one of the deepest V-shaped gorges, offering steep cliffs and untouched forests. Sandankyo Gorge in Hiroshima Prefecture features numerous waterfalls and deep pools. Ryujin Gorge in Ibaraki Prefecture is home to one of Japan's longest pedestrian suspension bridges, offering panoramic views.

What natural features can I expect to see in Japan's canyons?

Japan's canyons showcase diverse natural beauty. You can find steep cliffs, emerald green waters, dense virgin forests, and unique rock formations. Many gorges feature waterfalls, such as the Kairo Falls in Dakigaeri Gorge, and deep pools. Some, like [Rankyo Gorge](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/7386729), are carved by rivers and offer spectacular views of rugged mountains and rapids.

Are there canyons in Japan suitable for families?

Yes, several canyons offer family-friendly experiences. Kurobe Gorge is popular for its scenic railway, the Kurobe Gorge Railway, which provides a comfortable way to see the gorge. Sandankyo Gorge has well-maintained walking trails suitable for various fitness levels, and boat tours are available in areas like Kurobuchi. Hatonosu Canyon in Tokyo also offers a promenade and refreshing waters for swimming in summer.

What is the best time of year to visit canyons in Japan?

The scenery in Japan's canyons changes dramatically with the seasons. Spring brings lush greenery and blooming flowers like azaleas, while autumn offers spectacular displays of red and yellow foliage, making it a particularly popular time. Summer provides opportunities for swimming and enjoying cooler temperatures within the gorges. Some areas, like Dakigaeri Gorge, even host fall foliage festivals.

How accessible are Japan's canyons by public transport?

Many canyons in Japan are accessible, with some being quite convenient. Hatonosu Canyon and Todoroki Valley are both easily reachable by train from central Tokyo. The Kurobe Gorge Railway provides direct access into [Kurobe Gorge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurobe_Gorge). For others, a combination of train and local bus services might be required, or a car rental for more remote locations.

Can I go canyoning (sawanobori) in Japan, and where?

Yes, canyoning, known as 'sawanobori' or 'shower climbing' in Japan, is a popular adventure activity. Minakami in Gunma Prefecture is considered a premier canyoning destination globally, offering courses from family-friendly to adrenaline-pumping. Nametoko Gorge in Shikoku and Kamoshika Canyon in Hakuba (Nagano Prefecture) are also renowned for their canyoning opportunities, featuring slides, waterfall descents, and swimming in deep pools.

Are there any historical or cultural sites associated with Japan's canyons?

Yes, some canyons have historical or cultural significance. [Iwaya-ji (Temple 45)](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/5771116), a religious building located in a gorge on Kuma Highland, is part of the Shikoku Pilgrimage and is known for its location embedded in a cliff. Todoroki Valley in Tokyo features the atmospheric Todoroki Fudo temple and remains of tunnel tombs. The Kurobe Gorge Railway itself has historical roots as an industrial railroad for hydroelectric power plant construction.

What kind of outdoor activities can I do near Japan's canyons?

Beyond exploring the canyons themselves, you can find various outdoor activities nearby. For cycling enthusiasts, there are routes like the 'Tatara Bridge – Kurushima-Kaikyō Bridge loop' or the 'Peach blossom tour through the mountain hamlet of Wazo'. Mountain biking is also popular, with trails such as the '七国峠 loop from 飯能'. Additionally, running trails like the 'Imperial Palace Loop, Tokyo' offer scenic routes. You can find more details on these activities in the [MTB Trails in Japan](https://www.komoot.com/guide/71996/mtb-trails-in-japan), [Cycling in Japan](https://www.komoot.com/guide/71998/cycling-in-japan), and [Running Trails in Japan](https://www.komoot.com/guide/73365/running-trails-in-japan) guides.

Where can I find unique viewpoints within Japan's canyons?

Many canyons offer stunning viewpoints. The Ryujin Suspension Bridge in Ryujin Gorge provides panoramic views of the gorge, surrounding mountain ranges, and even the Mito cityscape. The Kurobe Gorge Railway offers continuous scenic views as it traverses bridges and tunnels. The Kami-no-Iwahashi Bridge in Dakigaeri Gorge, Akita's oldest suspension bridge, also provides excellent vantage points. For a challenging view, [Sanpuku-gake Cliff](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/6831609) offers a dramatic perspective.

What do visitors particularly enjoy about the canyons in Japan?

Visitors appreciate the diverse experiences offered by Japan's canyons. Many enjoy the thrill of boat rides through gorges like [Rankyo Gorge](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/7386729) or the scenic train journey through Kurobe Gorge. The vibrant autumn foliage is a consistent highlight. For adventurous visitors, challenging routes like the [Narrow Rock Passage](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/732803) are considered fun, despite potential muddy conditions. The serene escape from urban life, even within Tokyo at places like Todoroki Valley, is also highly valued.

Are there any specific permits required for visiting or canyoning in Japan?

For general visits to most scenic gorges, specific permits are typically not required, though some areas might have entrance fees or require tickets for specific attractions like boat tours or scenic railways. For adventurous activities like canyoning (sawanobori), especially in more remote or challenging areas, it's highly recommended to go with an organized tour operator who will handle any necessary permits or access arrangements. Always check local regulations for the specific area you plan to visit.

What are some of the geological characteristics of Japan's canyons?

Japan's canyons are largely shaped by rivers and tectonic activity, resulting in diverse geological features. Many are deep V-shaped gorges, like [Kurobe Gorge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurobe_Gorge), carved through mountainous terrain. You'll find conglomerate rock formations, as seen at [Iwaya-ji (Temple 45)](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/5771116), and smooth granite rocks in places like Nametoko Gorge. The striking cobalt-blue color of the water in Dakigaeri Gorge is attributed to highly acidic water from upstream hot springs, showcasing unique mineral interactions.

Which canyons offer opportunities for wild swimming?

While not explicitly designated as 'wild swimming' spots, several canyons in Japan feature clear, refreshing waters where visitors can cool off. Hatonosu Canyon in Tokyo is noted for its refreshing, cold waters, making it a great spot for swimming during the summer. Canyoning activities in places like Minakami, Nametoko Gorge, and Kamoshika Canyon also involve swimming in deep pools as part of the adventure.

WORLD-CLASS EXPERIENCES UNDER TWO HOURS FROM TOKYO AND OSAKA

![](https://img2.storyblok.com/2000x0/f/96479/800x500/b1997de7e9/rafting-tours.jpg)

### [Rafting](https://canyons.jp/en/areas/minakami/minakami-rafting)

* * *

The Spring Season brings world-class Grade 4+ whitewater and high thrills. The Summer Season involves playing inside and outside the raft on a mellow Grade 1-2 section.

The two seasons are very different in terms of distance covered on the river and the type of experience, so think about your ideal thrill level before you pick.

Canyons rafting tours are only available in Minakami.

[Family Rafting](https://canyons.jp/en/tour-product/minakami/rafting/summer-rafting)

[Rafting \[Minakami\]](https://canyons.jp/en/tours/rafting/minakami-rafting-tours)

[Private Rafting Tour](https://canyons.jp/en/tours/private-tours)

![](https://img2.storyblok.com/2000x0/f/96479/800x500/4fbb250d3c/canyoning-tours.jpg)

### [Canyoning](https://canyons.jp/en/tours/canyoning/canyoning-tours)

* * *

If you haven't tried canyoning yet, Japan is an amazing location to get into this adventure sport.

Imagine crystal clear water, pure air, amazing views at every turn, and world-class canyons.

Our two main areas of Minakami and Okutama are both under 90 minutes from Tokyo.

[Family Canyoning](https://canyons.jp/en/tour-product/minakami/canyoning/family-Canyoning)

[Canyoning \[Minakami\]](https://canyons.jp/en/areas/minakami/minakami-canyoning)

[Private Canyoning Tours](https://canyons.jp/en/tours/private-tours)

![](https://img2.storyblok.com/2000x0/f/96479/800x500/f7bb21dffe/pack-rafting-tours.jpg)

### [Packrafting](https://canyons.jp/en/tours/pack-raft/packrafting-tours)

* * *

Packrafting involves moving downriver on a single-person inflatable kayak.

It requires a decent level of fitness and swimming ability.

At Canyons, we use a level system. Level 1-2 is suitable for first-time packrafters to learn the basics and Level 3 or above is best for people with double-blade (kayaking) experience.

[Packrafting](https://canyons.jp/en/tours/pack-raft/packrafting-tours)

[Private Packrafting Tour](https://canyons.jp/en/tours/private-tours)

![](https://img2.storyblok.com/2000x0/f/96479/500x499/982e2489c9/accom_glamp_bell_tent.jpg)

### [Glamping & Combo Tours](https://canyons.jp/en/areas/minakami/minakami-glamping-riverside-oasis)

* * *

If you want to try both rafting and canyoning, then one of combo tours will be a perfect fit!

Minakami is known as an outdoor paradise with many outdoor activities on offer there. Why not stay for the night?

By combining activities, you also get awesome discounts with between 15-20% off the normal cost.

[Glamping \[Minakami\]](https://canyons.jp/en/areas/minakami/minakami-glamping-riverside-oasis)

[Package deals \[Minakami\]](https://canyons.jp/en/tours/value-combo/all-combo-tours)

[BBQ \[Minakami\]](https://canyons.jp/en/areas/minakami/barbecue)

[Lunch Options \[Minakami\]](https://canyons.jp/en/areas/minakami/lunch)

## CANYONS WINTER ADVENTURES

AMAZING SNOW - NO CROWDS

![](https://img2.storyblok.com/2000x0/f/96479/800x500/72a14539d9/minakami-ski-lessons.jpg)

### [Ski & Snowboard school](https://canyons.jp/en/winter-tours/snowsports-school)

Canyons operates schools in 4 areas of Japan; Minakami, Yuzawa, Nozawa, Myoko. Our international team of experienced instructors can help you to the next level whether you are a first timer or expert.

[Minakami Ski School](https://canyons.jp/en/winter-tours/hodaigi-ski-resort)

[Nozawa Ski School](https://canyons.jp/en/winter-tours/nozawa-onsen-ski-resort)

[Yuzawa Ski School](https://canyons.jp/en/winter-tours/ishiuchi-maruyama-ski-school)

[Naspa Ski School](https://canyons.jp/en/winter-tours/naspa-ski-garden)

[Myoko Ski School](https://canyons.jp/en/winter-tours/myoko)

![](https://img2.storyblok.com/2000x0/f/96479/800x500/2f3469a787/snowcany-tours.jpg)

### [Snow Canyoning](https://canyons.jp/en/winter-tours/snow-canyoning)

Canyons are the only company in the world to offer this dynamic new sport. A mix of canyoning, sledding and mountaineering combine to create an incredible powder snow experience.

[Snow Canyoning](https://canyons.jp/en/winter-tours/snow-canyoning)

![](https://img2.storyblok.com/2000x0/f/96479/1200x550/9597690a8e/tours_winter_backcountrytours_header.jpg)

### [Backcountry tour](https://canyons.jp/en/winter-tours/snowshoe-tour)

Looking for the best backcountry skiing in Japan? Canyons offers unforgettable guided ski tours to Japan’s hidden powder stashes, with over 20 years of experience in safely leading skiers and snowboarders through some of the most epic terrain the country has to offer.

[Backcountry](https://canyons.jp/en/winter-tours/backcountry-tours)

![](https://img2.storyblok.com/2000x0/f/96479/5504x3096/b5dd89e727/winter-package.JPG)

### [Winter Packages](https://canyons.jp/en/areas/minakami/minakami-snow-glamping-riverside-oasis)

Our winter packages provide the perfect escape to reconnect with nature, recharge, and embrace the thrill of Japan's legendary winter conditions.

[Winter packages](https://canyons.jp/en/winter-tours/winter-packages)

## THE CANYONS DIFFERENCE

WORLD-CLASS GUIDES MEANS WORLD-CLASS TOURS

![](https://img2.storyblok.com/2000x0/f/96479/1460x1461/e16d75dd9c/mike.jpg)

* * *

##### **A MESSAGE FROM MIKE**

Outdoor adventure is not just a job for us, it's our passion.

We strive every day to achieve our company mission to "Refresh the world through adventure experiences" by providing world-class experiences that:

\\* Maximise **fun** and **excitement**

\\* Facilitate **connection with nature** and **local culture**

\\* Advance personal growth (physical, mental and spiritual)

Our international team of professional guides will show you the beauty of the REAL Japan whilst on the experience of a lifetime.

web.markdown:
![Thumbnail (1920x1080)](https://i.ytimg.com/vi_webp/mrmxZYdH7bw/maxresdefault.webp)
# [The Best Way to Spend Summer in Japan? CANYONING & HIKING in Gunma](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mrmxZYdH7bw)

**Visibility**: Public
**Uploaded by**: [Roy and Aimee | Japan Outdoors](https://www.youtube.com/@RoyandAimee)
**Uploaded at**: 2023-07-22
**Published at**: 
**Length**: 08:54
**Views**: 2874
**Likes**: 85
**Category**: People & Blogs

## Description

```
Summer in Japan is hot so we decided to cool down and get the heart racing with some canyoning! We went on a weekend trip to the prefecture of Gunma, 2-3 hours north-west of Tokyo, to hike Mt. Akagi, visit a firefly festival and try to conquer a canyon for the first time. 

//COME SAY HI!
Patreon (free behind the scenes content!): https://www.patreon.com/RoyandAimee
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/royandaimee/

//TRAVEL INFO: 
Canyons Japan - https://canyons.jp/en
Mt. Akagi - https://www.japan.travel/en/spot/2077/
Firefly Festival - https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/02301-t5670/
Sanazawa Terrace Onsen - https://enjoy-minakami.com/en/spa/spa15-en-6-35-14-2-2-2.html

//MUSIC FROM: 
Epidemic Sound - https://www.epidemicsound.com/referral/zjyf0a/

//CHAPTERS: 
0:00 Intro
0:19 Hiking Mt. Akagi, Gunma
3:38 Why travel to Gunma?
4:11 Firefly Festival 
5:36 Canyons Japan
8:36 Outro

#japan #travel #canyoning #hiking
```

## Transcript

We have got an action packed weekend ahead of us.
We have got canyoning.
We have got hiking.
We have got a... Firefly Festival? So let's not waste any more time let's get into it!
Lets go!
Let's go!
For our first stop on our Gunma adventure we have come to Mount Akagi
to hike it! It's a relatively easy three and a half hours. It's also one of Japan's 100
famous mountains, so let's get going!
Wowie - these are the sounds of summer, hey?
Yeah...
Do you know what mountains out there what mountain range it is?
Ooh it's flattened out now. Look! I think we're on a ridgeline. yeah
Now it's nice and easy.
We made it - to the summit already. It was so quick. Just an hour, ne? Yeah we just like powered
through everyone and then here we are. Maybe there's a viewing spot just down that way, so let's go!
For a quick snack I've got jelly cup with fruit, and a whole chicken slab sausage thing.
It's the first time I'm having this hopefully it's not too.....not too bad.
We've made it to the second, but a little bit lower peak - Komagatake - the first one was Kurobi.
The scenery is just beautiful. Today we have a fantastic clear day.
What else can you say? Amazing! Beautiful! The mountain just keeps giving doesn't it?
Just keeps giving. Incredible. Easy to reach from Tokyo get here by public transport.
What more could you want? Easy hike. Easy access.
You a salesperson now?
I'm a sales person for mountains.
As we drive on to our next destination let me tell you a little bit more about Gunma.
This prefecture is a two to three hour drive from Tokyo and despite being very nice, in
our opinion, it consistently ranks in the bottom fourth of most attractive prefectures in Japan.
Out of 47! Poor Gunma. I mean really, it's got everything - beautiful nature, some of the
best Onsen in Japan and as we'll find out soon some pretty insane canyoning so we think
it makes a great side trip from Tokyo.
So we've kind of just wrapped up the evening
with a wonderful Onsen in this this beautiful place next to the rice fields and then we
followed up with a really good meal.
And now, we're at the final thing for the day which
is a firefly... what to call it? Event. I mean we actually don't have any experience with
fire flies besides maybe catching one or two in Tears of the Kingdom.
But they only come out in June so I guess now is the prime time to go see them.
So before going to this Firefly Festival we naively thought we'd be able to catch beautiful shots
like this to show you guys. However we discovered filming fireflies is hard, and this is the
best we got. There were actually quite a few and ambience was great in amongst the rice
fields but you'll have to use your imagination a little.
Things are looking pretty cozy. It IS cozy but actually we're trying to cool the van down tonight because it's
a scorcher. All right what well, we'll see you bright and early in the morning for more adventures.
Good morning we went and cleared at 7-Eleven last night so we could have a quick
breakfast of many different things and then we're going to go on our Canyoning Adventure.
Are you gonna... show us your outfit?
3 - 2 - 1 JUMP!
[screams]
[unmanly screams]
[onlookers laughing]
Have fun!
If you're looking for outdoor adventure in Japan we really can't recommend
Canyon's Japan enough. They do rafting as well as canyoning and anyone from complete beginners
like us can do it. We'll leave links to all the places we visited in the video description.
Thank you for joining us on another scorching hot summer fun. We actually got these from
the Firefly event by the way they're drawn by school kids, how cool is that? Anyway that's
all we have in store for this video thank you so much for joining us and we'll see you
in the next one. Bye

### Gorges
[Takachiho Gorge•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e8052.html)

The [Takachiho Gorge](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e8052.html) in [Miyazaki Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1245.html) is a narrow gorge lined with sheer cliffs and a 17 meter high waterfall along the way.

[Kurobe Gorge•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7575.html)

web.markdown:
![](https://www.japan-guide.com/thumb/interest_nature.jpg)

Many visitors to Japan limit their sightseeing activities to the country's heavily urbanized areas between [Tokyo](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2164.html), [Kyoto](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2158.html) and [Hiroshima](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2160.html). As a result, many return home with a hardened misconception that Japan is one large, densely populated megacity. In fact, however, over two thirds of Japan are covered by forested mountains and hills, compared to less than ten percent residential and industrial land.

The Japanese archipelago stretches nearly 3000 kilometers from north to south, allowing visitors to experience a wide range of natural sights from the [drift ice](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6860.html) in the seas off [Hokkaido](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1101.html) to the mangrove jungles in [Okinawa](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1247.html). In between, there are majestic [volcanoes](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2327.html), breathtaking coastlines and vast forests inhabited by monkeys, bears, deer, cranes and other wildlife. Places of particular natural beauty are protected as [national parks](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2325.html) and [World Heritage Sites](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2251.html).

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g20/2122_02.jpg)

Mangroves on Iriomote

The following is a short selection of some of the best natural sites in Japan:

### Mountains and volcanoes

Japan has a mountainous interior which is mostly made up of [volcanoes](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2327.html). These heights provide plenty of [hiking](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2427.html) opportunities and scenic viewpoints from which to see the surrounding areas.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe2172_225.jpg)













[Yamanashi](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1213.html) and [Shizuoka](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1218.html) prefectures



[Mount Fuji•••](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2172.html)

[Mount Fuji](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2172.html) is a beautifully symmetrical [volcano](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2327.html), and the symbol and highest mountain of Japan. [Climbing Mount Fuji](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6901.html) is popular during summer with people ascending via four different trails. The [Fuji Five Lakes](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6900.html) region at the northern foot of Mount Fuji and [Hakone](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e5200.html) are popular resort destinations with [views of the mountain](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6933.html).

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe3029_225.jpg)













[Tokyo](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2164.html)



[Takaosan•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3029.html)

[Mount Takao](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3029.html) is one of the closest natural recreation areas to central [Tokyo](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2164.html) offering beautiful scenery, an interesting [temple](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2058.html) and attractive [hiking](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2427.html) opportunities. Visitors can choose to hike all the way up to the summit or take the cablecar or chair lift halfway up.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe4552_225.jpg)













[Aso](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4550.html)



[Mount Aso•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4552.html)

[Mount Aso](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4552.html) lies in the center of [Kyushu](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1108.html) and is part of the [Aso-Kuju National Park](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4570.html). Its caldera is one of the largest in the world with a diameter of about 25 kilometers and a circumference of over 100 kilometers. Nakadake Crater at the center of the caldera is easily visited but not always accessible due to volcanic activities.


### Capes, coasts and beaches

Japan's coastline is one of the world's longest, and many sections of it are quite impressive. Not only are there rugged cliffs, geological formations and [hiking trails](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2427.html), but there are also plenty of [beaches](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2461.html) offering swimming and [snorkeling](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2424_snorkeling.html) opportunities.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe5034_225.jpg)













[Sanriku Coast](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e5025.html)



[Kitayamazaki Coast•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e5034.html)


The [Kitayamazaki Coast](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e5034.html) is an eight kilometer long stretch of coastline in northern [Iwate Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1204.html) featuring sheer, 150-200 meter high cliffs. The coast is best seen from the Kitayamazaki Observatory, a park at the northern end of the coastline.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe6308_225.jpg)













[Izu Peninsula](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6310.html)



[Jogasaki Coast](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6308.html)


The [Jogasaki Coast](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6308.html) is a beautiful section of coastline along the [Izu Peninsula](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6310.html)'s eastern shore. There is an attractive hiking trail that follows the coast for almost ten kilometers, offering beautiful views of the jagged cliffs and stone formations along the edge.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe3729_225.jpg)













[Shimokita Peninsula](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3725.html)



[Cape Oma](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3729.html)

[Cape Oma](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3729.html) is the northernmost point of the [Shimokita Peninsula](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3725.html) and of the entire Honshu Island, Japan's main island. The cape looks across over the Tsugaru Kaikyo Strait to southern [Hokkaido](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1101.html) where the city of Hakodate is visible on clear days. The area is most famous for the large tuna caught in its waters.


### Gorges

Many gorges with beautiful views of cliffs, forests and waterfalls can be found in Japan. Many of the gorges can be [hiked](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2427.html), while others can be enjoyed from [boat tours or sightseeing trains](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2466.html).

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe8052_225.jpg)













[Takachiho](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e8050.html)



[Takachiho Gorge•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e8052.html)


The [Takachiho Gorge](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e8052.html) in [Miyazaki Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1245.html) is a narrow gorge lined with sheer cliffs and a 17 meter high waterfall along the way. Visitors can rent row boats to paddle down the river through the gorge or walk along paved paths that run along its edges.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe7575_225.jpg)













[Toyama Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1219.html)



[Kurobe Gorge•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7575.html)


The [Kurobe Gorge](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7575.html) is a beautiful, forested ravine in the rugged mountains of the [Northern Japanese Alps](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6043.html). It is one of the deepest gorges in Japan with steep, nearly vertical cliffs, untouched virgin forests and outdoor [hot springs](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2292.html). The main attraction is the sightseeing train that operates twenty kilometers into the gorge.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe5006_225.jpg)













[Near Hiraizumi](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e5000.html)



[Geibikei Gorge](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e5006.html)


The [Geibikei Gorge](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e5006.html) is a spectacular natural site outside [Hiraizumi](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e5000.html) in the interior of [Iwate Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1204.html). The best way to view the tall cliffs and rock formations in the gorge is to take a 90-minute ride on a flat-bottomed boat that leads about one kilometer in.


### Caves

Large limestone caves can be found across Japan and offer natural formations like limestone pools, underground waterfalls and streams that were formed millions of years ago. Visitors can explore a portion of these caves via walking courses and marvel at their natural beauty.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe6130_225.jpg)













[Yamaguchi Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1239.html)



[Akiyoshido•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6130.html)

[Akiyoshido Cave](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6130.html) in [Yamaguchi Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1239.html) is one of Japan's largest and longest limestone caves. One kilometer of the nine kilometer long cave is open to the public, and various natural formations like limestone pools, underground waterfalls and streams, can be seen.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe7793_225.jpg)













[Fukushima Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1208.html)



[Abukumado•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7793.html)

[Abukumado Cave](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7793.html) is a 3000 meter limestone cave network in eastern [Fukushima Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1208.html) that was formed over 80 million years ago. About 600 meters of the caverns are opened to the public, and it takes about an hour to explore the main walking course.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe5028_225.jpg)













[Sanriku Coast](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e5025.html)



[Ryusendo Cave](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e5028.html)


Regarded as one of Japan's three great limestone caves, [Ryusendo](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e5028.html) extends nearly 5000 meters into the mountains of Iwaizumi Town in [Iwate Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1204.html). About 700 meters of the cave are open to the public, and visitors can walk along the underground river and view three of the cave's four underground lakes.


### Marshlands

Marshlands are popular [hiking destinations](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2427.html) found both up in the mountains and in lower elevations. Many marshlands are particularly beautiful during the [autumn color](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2014.html) season.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe7440_225.jpg)













[Gunma Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1209.html)



[Oze National Park•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7440.html)

[Oze National Park](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7440.html) is an excellent [hiking](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2427.html) destination that is popular during the skunk cabbages blooming season in late spring and early summer and during the [fall colors](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2014.html) if autumn. There are numerous trailheads to access the well maintained trails that lead around the marshlands and park.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe3811_225.jpg)













[Nikko](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3800.html)



[Senjogahara Marsh•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3811.html)


The [Senjogahara Marshland](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3811.html) covers the plateau between [Lake Chuzenji](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3806.html) and [Yumoto Onsen](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3807.html). It offers some of the best hiking in Nikko National Park and is particularly beautiful during the [autumn leaf](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2014.html) season in October.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe6792_225.jpg)













[Hokkaido](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1101.html)



[Kushiro Marshlands](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6792.html)


The [Kushiro Marshland](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6792.html) in eastern [Hokkaido](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1101.html) is a [national park](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2325.html) supporting the only known population of endangered Japanese cranes in the country. The park offers bird watching, nature viewing and walking trails.


### Waterfalls

There are hundreds of waterfalls across Japan, and some of them, like the [Nachi Waterfall](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4955.html), have been religious sites with long histories. Some waterfalls can only be accessed by [hiking](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2427.html) along nature trails, while others can be conveniently viewed from observation decks.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe4955_225.jpg)













[Kumano](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4950.html)



[Nachi Waterfall••](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4955.html)


At 133 meters tall, [Nachi Waterfall](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4955.html) (Nachi no Taki) is the tallest single-tiered waterfall in Japan and is ranked as one of Japan's three most beautiful falls. Nachi no Taki was the original religious site in the [Kumano Region](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4950.html) and was venerated by the earliest Japanese people.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe7120_225.jpg)













[Okinawa Honto](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7101.html)



[Hiji Waterfall•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7120.html)

[Hiji Waterfall](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7120.html) is a 26 meter tall waterfall located in the northern [Yambaru area](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7131.html) of [Okinawa Honto](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7101.html). The waterfall is at the end of a nature trail through the forest and is a good spot for a rest before making the return trip back.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe3812_225.jpg)













[Nikko](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3800.html)



[Kegon Waterfall](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3812.html)


The almost 100 meter tall [Kegon Waterfall](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3812.html) is the most famous of [Nikko](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3800.html)'s many beautiful waterfalls, and ranked as one of Japan's three most beautiful falls. The waterfall is also a popular [autumn color](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2014.html) spot around mid to late October.


### Rivers

There are many rivers in Japan, and some of them can be explored by river cruises. Other rivers are lined by [hiking trails](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2427.html) allowing visitors to enjoy the scenery at their own pace.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe7225_225.jpg)













[Yaeyama Islands](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7200.html)



[Iriomote Island•••](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7225.html)


Most of [Iriomote Island](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7225.html)'s interior is covered in dense jungle accessible by [rivers](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7225.html) that head inland from the sea. Kayak tours are offered on several of the rivers, while jungle boat cruises are organized on the island's two longest rivers.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe3775_225.jpg)













[Towada](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3776.html)



[Oirase Stream•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3775.html)


The [Oirase Stream](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3775.html) is a picturesque mountain stream in [Aomori Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1202.html) that is one of Japan's most famous and popular [autumn colors](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2014.html) destinations. Visitors can choose to hike, drive or take a bus to enjoy the views along the stream.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe3966_225.jpg)













[Kyoto](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2158.html)



[Hozugawa Cruise](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3966.html)


The [Hozugawa River](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3966.html) allows visitors to see the natural scenery of the largely undeveloped ravine from Kameoka to [Arashiyama](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3912.html) by joining a sightseeing cruise on traditional, flat-bottomed boats piloted by boatmen using oars and bamboo poles. The cruise is popularly combined with a ride on the [Sagano Scenic Railway](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3965.html).


### Lakes

There are a variety of lakes in Japan including caldera lakes, subterranean lakes and lagoons. Often surrounded by beautiful scenery, many lakes are popular [hiking](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2427.html) destinations, and some of them also offer sightseeing cruises.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe3778_225.jpg)













[Towada](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3776.html)



[Lake Towada•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3778.html)

[Lake Towada](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3778.html) is the largest caldera lake on Honshu, Japan's main island, and is characterized by its two peninsulas. The best way to see the lake is by [sightseeing cruises](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3778.html) which offer close up views of the peninsulas, while the shores of the lake and the nearby [Oirase Stream](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3775.html) offer beautiful [autumn colors](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2014.html) around late October.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe6802_225.jpg)













[Akan National Park](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6800.html)



[Lake Mashu•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6802.html)

[Lake Mashu](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6802.html) is a caldera lake in the [Akan National Park](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6800.html). It is widely considered to be Japan's most beautiful lake, and also vies for the position of being the clearest lake in the world. Visitors are not allowed to go down to the water, but can view it from two observation decks stationed along the rim of the caldera.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe6853_225.jpg)













[Shiretoko Peninsula](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6850.html)



[Shiretoko Five Lakes•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6853.html)


The [Shiretoko Five Lakes](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6853.html) are a set of five small lakes that offer beautiful views of the surrounding mountains and wilderness in [Shiretoko](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6850.html). Visitors can walk along an elevated boardwalk to enjoy views of the first lake, while nature trails lead around the others.


### Bays

Bays have been admired for their scenic beauty for centuries, and even hold the three top spots on the famed list of [Japan's three most scenic places](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2250.html).

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe7201_225.jpg)













[Yaeyama Islands](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7200.html)



[Kabira Bay•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7201.html)


Emerald blue Kabira Bay (Kabirawan) is considered [Ishigaki Island](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7201.html)'s most scenic view. Swimming, [snorkeling](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2424_snorkeling.html) and [diving](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2424_diving.html) in the bay are not allowed, but a touristy, 30-minute glass bottom boat ride lets you take a look at the bay's underwater world.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe5101_225.jpg)













[Matsushima](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e5100.html)



[Matsushima Bay•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e5101.html)

[Matsushima Bay](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e5101.html) is dotted by over 200 small islands covered by pine trees and has been celebrated as one of [Japan's three most scenic views](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2250.html) for hundreds of years. The best way to enjoy the bay is by joining a sightseeing cruise.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe4307_225.jpg)













[Shima Peninsula](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4310.html)



[Ago Bay](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4307.html)

[Ago Bay](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4307.html) at the southern tip of the [Shima Peninsula](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4310.html), is a scenic, island-dotted bay with a rugged coastline. The bay is famous for pearl cultivation, and countless oyster rafts can be seen floating on the water. There are also sightseeing boat cruises that gives visitors a closer view of the smaller islands around the bay.


### Others

Below are a few other unique natural attractions found in Japan:

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe3992_225.jpg)













[Amanohashidate](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3990.html)



[Amanohashidate Sandbar•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3992.html)


The [Amanohashidate Sandbar](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3992.html) is a beautiful, three kilometer long isthmus that spans Miyazu Bay in northern [Kyoto Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1226.html). The sandbar is lined with about 8000 pine trees, and the view of the sandbar from the mountains at either end of the bay has been admired for centuries as one of Japan's [three most scenic views](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2250.html).

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe8102_225.jpg)













[Tottori](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e8100.html)



[Tottori Sand Dunes•](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e8102.html)


The [Tottori Sand Dunes](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e8102.html) are the largest sand dunes in Japan and [Tottori](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e8100.html)'s most famous tourist attraction. The sand dunes are about 16 kilometers long, up to two kilometers wide and 50 meters high. The nearby [sand museum](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e8102.html) displays large sculptures made of sand.

- ![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g6/XYZeXYZe7852_225.jpg)













[Naruto](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7850.html)



[Naruto Whirlpools](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7852.html)


The [Naruto Whirlpools](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7852.html) in the Naruto Strait are created by the large volumes of water moving between the [Seto Inland Sea](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e5445.html) and the Pacific Ocean between high and low tide, combined with the unique underwater geography of the narrow strait. Visitors can join sightseeing cruises to get right up next to and among the whirlpools.

### A photo spot with arts and a great view
Kiyotsukyo Gorge, known as one of Japan's three great gorges along with Kurobe Gorge and Osugi Gorge, was designated as Joshinetsu Kogen National Park in September 1949, and is a treasure house of academic materials.

Kiyotsukyo Gorge, known as one of Japan's three great gorges along with Kurobe Gorge and Osugi Gorge, was designated as Joshinetsu Kogen National Park in September 1949, and is a treasure house of academic materials.

The gigantic rock walls cut across the river create a V-shaped grand canyon that is the pride of the nation, and is designated as a national natural monument of scenic beauty.

The combination of the majestic columnar-jointed rock surfaces and the clear rapids of the Kiyotsu River is dynamic and amazing, and leaves a deep impression on visitors.

The Kiyotsukyo Valley Tunnel was reopened as the artwork “Tunnel of Light” by the Chinese architectural unit “Ma Yansong / MAD Architects” at the 7th Echigo-Tsumari Art Triennale (2018).

As you proceed through the cave-inspired entrance, you will find many mechanisms to not only see nature, but also to see it from a different perspective, such as a passageway of light effects and a space lined with distorted mirrors.

The highlight is the panoramic station at the far end of the tunnel. The walls are made of stainless steel plates and the floor is covered with water, reflecting the grand canyon.

# Japan’s Most Stunning Canyons and Gorges: A Complete Guide for 2026

Forget everything you think you know about dramatic canyons. Japan doesn’t need the Grand Canyon to steal your breath away. Its gorges are tighter, greener, and wrapped in centuries of mythology — the kind of place where mist clings to mossy walls and you can hear your own footsteps echoing off basalt columns.

Whether you’re a landscape photographer chasing emerald water or a hiker craving solitude, Japan’s canyon country delivers in ways most travelers never expect.

## Why Japan’s Canyons Hit Different

Here’s the thing — Japanese gorges trade raw scale for intimacy. You don’t stare down from a rim. You walk _through_ them. Your fingers brush ancient stone. Birdsong bounces off cliff faces. Many of these places carry samurai legends, folk tales, and spiritual weight that turns a simple hike into something deeper.

The geology is no joke either. Volcanic eruptions, tectonic shifts, and millennia of river carving have produced everything from columnar basalt walls to granite chasms with water so green it looks filtered. And the seasonal shifts? Spring brings fresh green and azaleas. Autumn sets the whole valley on fire with red and gold. Summer lets you swim in surprisingly cold, crystal-clear pools.

## Top Canyons You Can’t Miss

### Takachiho Gorge — Miyazaki Prefecture, Kyushu

This is the one that keeps showing up on every “best of Japan” list, and for good reason. The Gokase River carved a narrow canyon through columnar basalt left behind by ancient volcanic eruptions. The walls rise nearly 100 meters on both sides — perfectly geometric, almost unreal. Manai Falls drops 17 meters into emerald water below, and the whole scene looks like someone rendered it in CGI.

Getting there takes effort. No train station in Takachiho. You’ll need a rental car (about 2–3 hours from Mount Aso) or a highway bus from Kumamoto or Fukuoka. But the payoff is massive — especially on overcast days, when the deep gorge glows with moody light.

**Best time**: Late April through May for fresh greens, or mid-November for autumn color.

### Kurobe Gorge — Toyama Prefecture

Often called “Japan’s most dramatic gorge,” Kurobe Gorge earns that title honestly. Emerald-green water winds through granite cliffs, and the Kurobe Gorge Railway ride through it in autumn feels like traveling through a living painting. Seam hot springs nestle right in the cliff walls — you can spot steam rising from the rock face as the train curves through.

**Access**: Take the Toyama Chiho Railway to Unazuki Onsen Station, then hop on the Kurobe Gorge Railway. Straightforward and scenic.

### Iya Valley — Tokushima Prefecture, Shikoku

Vine suspension bridges. Mist-covered ravines. Remote mountain villages where defeated Heike samurai reportedly hid centuries ago. Iya Valley doesn’t just look mythical — it _feels_ mythical. The steep gorge walls and fog-soaked forests create a sense of timelessness that most places in Japan can’t match.

**Access**: Train or highway bus from Tokushima City to Oboke Station, then a local bus deeper into the valley.

### Ryuokyo Canyon — Nagano Prefecture

Tucked into the Japanese Alps, Ryuokyo Canyon sits along the Azusa River with cedar forests and towering rock walls. It’s a favorite among canyoning and packraft adventurers — the water is clear, the views are relentless, and the terrain ranges from accessible trails to serious technical routes.

**Nearby bonus**: Combine this with Kamikochi National Park for a multi-day alpine experience.

### Osugidani — Mie Prefecture

Sometimes compared to Yosemite, and not just for show. Osugidani features towering cliffs, pristine rivers, and the dramatic Nanatsugama-Godan Falls. Hikers cross narrow ridges, wander through mossy forests, and shuffle across suspension bridges. The terrain was nearly impossible to access until modern trails opened it up.

## Canyons Easy to Reach From Tokyo

Not everyone has two weeks. If you’re based in Tokyo and want a canyon fix without a long haul:

**Hatonosu Canyon** and **Todoroki Valley** are both reachable by train from central Tokyo. Todoroki Valley in particular offers a genuine escape from the city without leaving the metropolitan area. For something slightly further but still doable in a day, **Kanmangafuchi Abyss** near Nikko sits just over a kilometer from the famous shrines — a small gorge with its own waterfalls, whirlpools, and stone statues. Most tourists walk right past it. Don’t be most tourists.

## Seasonal Breakdown: When to Go

| Season | What You Get |
| --- | --- |
| **Spring (late Mar–May)** | Lush greenery, azaleas blooming, pleasant hiking temps |
| **Summer (Jun–Aug)** | Swimming in gorges, cooler temperatures inside the canyons, though June rainy season brings dramatic mountain fog |
| **Autumn (Oct–Nov)** | The peak season. Red and gold foliage across nearly every gorge — consistently the most photographed time |
| **Winter (Dec–Feb)** | Snow-dusted cliffs, fewer crowds, some routes close due to ice |

Late April through May and mid-November are the sweet spots for most gorges. If you can handle rain, June’s foggy mountain conditions create genuinely otherworldly photos — especially in places like Kumano Kodo’s Daimon-zaka staircase.

## Getting Around Canyon Country

Japan’s transport network makes most of these accessible, but the logistics vary:

- **Train + local bus** works for Kurobe Gorge, Iya Valley, and Kanmangafuchi
- **Rental car** is essential for Takachiho Gorge, Osugidani, and remote Tohoku gorges like Genbikei or Geibikei in Iwate
- **Shinkansen** gets you between major hubs fast — Tokyo to Toyama, Tokyo to Tokushima, all doable in a few hours

One practical note: if you’re driving between Takayama and Kanazawa via Shirakawa-go in winter, snow chains are non-negotiable. Roads are well-maintained but ice happens.

## What Makes These Places Stick With You

It’s not just the views — though the views are extraordinary. It’s the sound of water hitting stone in a narrow gorge. It’s the smell of cedar and wet moss. It’s the realization that samurai once stood where you’re standing, hiding from history in these same ravines.

Japan’s canyons don’t shout. They pull you in. And once you’re inside, the outside world simply stops mattering.

![](https://www.beautifulworld.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/ltsukushima-shine-in-a-Lake.jpg)

Japan remains a sought-after destination for tourists and explorers who are drawn to its distinctive ambiance and the allure of the land of the rising sun. It is widely acknowledged that Japan offers an unparalleled experience.

However, if you want to have a unique experience, we strongly recommend that you not only visit Tokyo and [Mount Fuji](https://www.beautifulworld.com/asia/japan/mount-fuji/). Japan has other unbelievable natural wonders that are definitely a must see! In this article we present some of the most amazing natural attractions that visitors to Japan shouldn’t miss!

## Discover the Majestic Peaks

Japan boasts a diverse range of mountains, including the world-famous Mount Fuji, a symbol of the nation’s strength and resilience. But it is not all about Fuji, the country has more breathtaking views and exhilarating hiking adventures like the Japanese Alps, Mount Takao, and Mount Hiei.

![](https://www.beautifulworld.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Mountains-in-Japan.jpg)

### Japanese Alps

[The Japanese Alps](https://www.beautifulworld.com/asia/japan/japanese-alps/) are home to fascinating trails, with the standout being the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route. Known as the “Roof of Japan” it offers a thrilling journey through tunnels, alpine lakes, and snow walls using cable cars, buses, and trains.

After taking in the breathtaking views, unwind in the region’s hot springs. The Japanese Alps are dotted with numerous hot spring resorts, such as Shibu Onsen and Okuhida Onsen, providing relaxation and rejuvenation. Don’t miss visiting the UNESCO World Heritage Sites of Shirakawa-go and Gokayama, known for their traditional farmhouses with steep thatched roofs. Winter is an especially magical time to visit, with snow-covered houses.

### Mount Takao

The main highlight of Mount Takao is its peak, which stands at 599 meters (1,965 feet). There are multiple hiking trails of varying difficulty levels to reach the top so everyone can choose their own based on their fitness level. The peak offers spectacular panoramic views of the surrounding landscapes, including Tokyo’s skyline on clear days.

Takaosan Yakuoin Temple is located near Mount Takao peak, and it is a Buddhist temple with a history spanning over 1,200 years. It is a popular pilgrimage site and offers a serene atmosphere for visitors to explore. The temple complex includes various buildings, statues, and a cemetery. Don’t miss the opportunity to try “shojin ryori” vegetarian Buddhist cuisine served in the temple’s restaurants.

### Mount Hiei

From Mount Hiei you can enjoy the view of Kyoto and Lake Biwa, the largest freshwater lake in Japan. On clear days, the vista extends far into the distance, offering a captivating perspective of the surrounding landscape.

You can find Enryaku-ji Temple on the slopes of Mount Hiei. It is a historic Buddhist temple complex that dates back over 1,200 years. It is registered as a UNESCO World Heritage site and holds great cultural and religious significance.

## Immerse Yourself in the Charm of National Parks

Japan is home to numerous national parks, each offering unique natural wonders. Discover the scenic beauty of Nikko National Park, with its stunning waterfalls, lakes, and ancient shrines. Experience the dramatic coastal cliffs and scenic trails of Shiretoko National Park, or marvel at the breathtaking landscapes of Akan-Mashu National Park, known for its volcanic activity and crystal-clear lakes.

![](https://www.beautifulworld.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Japanese-building-in-Nikko.jpg)

### Nikko National Park

Nikko National Park blends natural beauty and cultural significance. It houses Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples, including the iconic Toshogu Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

The park integrates religious structures in pristine surroundings. It offers diverse landscapes of forests, lakes (like Lake Chuzenji), waterfalls (like Kegon Falls), and mountains (Mount Nantai, Mount Nyoho, and Mount Shirane). Visitors can hike and enjoy breathtaking views. The park also features relaxing natural hot springs, such as Yumoto Onsen and Kinugawa Onsen, for a rejuvenating experience.

### Shiretoko National Park

Shiretoko National Park, (also) a UNESCO World Heritage site in Japan, is a pristine wilderness area. It features a stunning blend of rugged coastline, dense forests, cliffs, and mountains.

The park offers breathtaking views of the Sea of Okhotsk, dramatic waterfalls, and serene lakes. It is home to rare species like the endangered Blakiston’s fish owl, brown bears, and marine life. The Shiretoko Five Lakes provide beautiful mountain reflections and are perfect for nature walks. Outdoor activities include hiking, guided tours, kayaking, and wildlife cruises.

### Akan-Mashu National Park

Akan-Mashu National Park showcases volcanic landscapes with Mount Oakan, Mount Meakan, and Mount Akan-Fuji offering stunning views and hiking opportunities. The park is home to pristine lakes like Lake Akan, Lake Mashu, and Lake Kussharo. Lake Mashu is renowned for its crystal-clear water.

Marshlands, including Kushiro Marsh, provide a haven for bird species. Visitors can explore Ainu culture in traditional villages and enjoy Ainu crafts, music, and cuisine. The park’s hot springs, known as onsen, offer relaxation amidst nature. It is rich in biodiversity, with species like red-crowned cranes, Ezo deer, and Blakiston’s fish owls. The flora includes alpine flowers and unique volcanic-adapted plants.

As you can see Japan’s landscapes and national parks offer a tapestry of breathtaking beauty, showcasing the country’s harmonious relationship with nature. Whether it’s the majestic mountains, enchanting forests, or vibrant seasonal displays, each destination offers a unique opportunity to connect with the natural world.

By embracing Japan’s stunning landscapes, travelers can embark on an unforgettable journey of discovery and appreciation for the awe-inspiring beauty that nature has to offer. So don’t hesitate if you always wanted to visit this magical country!
